requestedActions.title: Read titles of work packages the connected person can access, including paginated results
Authorize the connected person's OpenProject account via developer-owned OAuth on their own instance

guide.summary: OpenProject documents developer OAuth app registration with the api_v3 scope, an authorization code flow, and bearer-token use. Documented work package listing uses GET /api/v3/work_packages with offset pagination and nextByOffset links. The api_v3 scope is broad, and no narrower read-only scope is documented. Authorization, token exchange, the listing request and pagination are unverified until tested on a representative instance.

findings.detail: OpenProject lets you create an OAuth application with a name, redirect URL, and scopes, then provides a Client ID and Client secret for later use.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to the developer-owned OAuth app used for customer instances

findings.title: Request the documented api_v3 scope
findings.detail: Scopes are selected at registration. api_v3 is the standard OpenProject API scope, and it is assumed when no scope is checked.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to the work package read request

evidence.quote: Set the Scopes that the OAuth client application will be able to access. Multiple selection is possible. If no scope is checked, per default api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the
standard OpenProject API, while bcf_v2_1 is specific to the BIM edition of OpenProject.

findings.title: OAuth token boundary is broad
findings.detail: The documented api_v3 grant covers the standard API. No narrower read-only scope is documented, so the token cannot be described as read-only. Read-only behavior must be enforced by the request design and verified by testing.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to all OAuth requests with this app

findings.title: Authorization code flow and bearer header
findings.detail: The authorization URL takes client_id, redirect_uri, scope and prompt=consent. The code is exchanged at the token endpoint, and the access token is sent as a Bearer header on API requests.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to connecting the customer's OpenProject account

evidence.quote: https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
--data code = <Authentication code> \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer <Token>' `

findings.title: Paginated collection requests
findings.detail: Collections may be paginated. Offset-based pages are requested with offset and pageSize, and nextByOffset gives the following page when offset pagination is available.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies when reading all accessible work packages

evidence.quote: Collections may be paginated, this means that a single response from the server will not contain all elements of the collection, but only a subset. In this case the client
can issue further requests to retrieve the remaining elements. There are two ways to access the result pages of a paginated collection:
nextByOffset Link to retrieve the following page of elements (offset based) when offset based available
